topic.name: Identifying the Pivot Columns of a Matrix

question.text: The row echelon form matrix $B$ is given below. What are its non-pivot columns? \[ B=\begin{bmatrix} 3 & 4 & 3 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 &0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $B$ has $4$ pivots in the $1$st, $2$nd, $4$th, and $5$th columns:

\[B=\begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{3} & 4 & 3 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{2} & 0 & -4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{3} &0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} \end{bmatrix}\]

Therefore, the only non-pivot column is the $3$rd column.

question.text: Determine the number of pivot columns of the matrix $B,$ given by \[ B=\begin{bmatrix} -2 &0 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & 1 & 4 &-2 & 0\\ 0 & -3 & -6 & 4 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & -3 &1 & -1 \end{bmatrix}. \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to convert $B$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} B &= \begin{bmatrix} -2 &0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 4 &-2 & 0\\ 0 & -3 & -6 & 4 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 1 & -1 \end{bmatrix} & R_3&:=R_3+3R_2 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} -2 &0 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & 1 & 4 &-2 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 6 & -2 & 2\\ 0 & 0 & -3 &1 & -1 \end{bmatrix} & R_4&:=R_4+\dfrac{1}{2}R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-2} &0 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & 4 &-2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 &\bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{ 6 }& -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $B$ has $3$ pivots, and therefore the number of pivot columns is $3.$

question.text: What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by \[ P= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}? \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to convert $P$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} P &= \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix} &R_2&\leftrightarrow R_3 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{2} & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{1} & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{5} \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $P$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $3$rd, and $4$th columns.

question.text: The row echelon form matrix $A$ is given below. What are its non-pivot columns? \[ A=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & -4 & 3 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 2 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & -3 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Remember that the pivots of a matrix in row echelon form are the first non-zero entries in each row of the matrix.

We can see that $A$ has $3$ pivots in the $2$nd, $4$th and $5$th columns:

\[A=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-4} & 3 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{2} & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-3} \end{bmatrix}\]

Therefore, the only non-pivot columns are the $1$st and $3$rd columns.

question.text: What are the pivot columns of the matrix $P,$ given by \[ P= \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 6 \end{bmatrix}? \]
question.explanation:
First, we need to convert $P$ to row echelon form:

\begin{align*} P &= \begin{bmatrix} 7 & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 6 \end{bmatrix} &R_3&\leftrightarrow R_4 \\[5pt] &\sim \begin{bmatrix} \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{7} & 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{-2} & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & \bbox[lightgray, 3pt]{6} \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \end{align*}

Looking at the row echelon form, we see that $P$ has $3$ pivots. In particular, the pivot columns are the $1$st, $2$nd, and $4$th columns.
